# Maya2C

> Maya2C is a layer-1 blockchain written in Rust, built on NIST post-quantum cryptography. Every transaction carries two signatures, ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s (FIPS 205), and is accepted only if both verify. Validators order blocks with DAG-BFT consensus (a certified DAG with the Bullshark commit rule); safety holds while at most f of n validators are Byzantine, with f = (n − 1) / 3 rounded down. Peer connections use ML-KEM (FIPS 203), with ML-KEM-1024 preferred and ML-KEM-768 accepted. Status: the public testnet, maya-testnet-1, is paused (stopped 2026-10-28 on purpose); mainnet has not launched; no external security audit has been completed. The code is Apache-2.0.

Use the FAQ for direct answers. Pages marked as design or research describe work that is not in the live node; the architecture vision page states the status of each subsystem.

## Start here

- [FAQ](https://maya2c.dev/guides/faq/): direct answers on what Maya2C is, its algorithms, finality, mining, mainnet status, audit status, and how to run a node or a wallet
- [Testnet](https://maya2c.dev/guides/testnet/): current status of maya-testnet-1 (paused), and what test coins are
- [Experience Maya2C](https://maya2c.dev/experience/): an in-browser walkthrough of post-quantum signatures and blocks

## How it works

- [Post-quantum signatures](https://maya2c.dev/guides/signatures/): the two signature schemes, why both must verify, and the parameter sets
- [Post-quantum comparison](https://maya2c.dev/guides/pq-comparison/): dated, sourced comparison with 18 other post-quantum chain entries (searched 2026-11-01); where others are ahead; mainnet not launched
- [Hybrid signatures](https://maya2c.dev/reference/hybrid-signatures/): the construction of transaction authorization
- [Consensus and finality](https://maya2c.dev/guides/consensus/): DAG-BFT, the commit rule, the fault bound, and what finality means in this network
- [Post-quantum transport](https://maya2c.dev/reference/pq-transport/): ML-KEM key exchange on peer connections, ML-KEM-1024 preferred with ML-KEM-768 fallback
- [How a transaction works](https://maya2c.dev/guides/transactions/): the checks a transaction passes, the fee rule, and 256-bit amounts
- [Mining and validators](https://maya2c.dev/guides/mining/): GPU mining status, and why miners do not order blocks
- [Invariants](https://maya2c.dev/reference/invariants/): the numbered properties the code must keep, each pinned by a test
- [Architecture vision](https://maya2c.dev/reference/architecture-vision/): the status (shipped, research, planned) of each subsystem
- [Security audit](https://maya2c.dev/reference/security-audit/): the automated security checks, what each one proves, and what it does not

## Run it

- [Quickstart](https://maya2c.dev/guides/quickstart/): build the node and a wallet, and start a one-validator chain on your machine
- [Help run the network](https://maya2c.dev/guides/help-run/): join the testnet with one command (applies when the testnet restarts)
- [Run a validator](https://maya2c.dev/guides/validators/): validator steps for maya-testnet-1 (applies when the testnet restarts)
- [Wallet integration](https://maya2c.dev/guides/wallet/): how a wallet holds keys, signs, sets nonces and fees, and talks to a gateway
- [Passkey unlock](https://maya2c.dev/guides/passkey-unlock/): a device passkey unlocks the locally encrypted post-quantum key via the WebAuthn PRF extension; it never signs transactions
- [API reference](https://maya2c.dev/guides/api/): JSON-RPC and REST endpoints of the public gateway
- [Compiling a contract](https://maya2c.dev/guides/contracts/): building a WASM contract for the Maya VM

## Live services

These are offline or report on a paused network while maya-testnet-1 is stopped.

- Status (measured uptime from block timestamps): https://status.maya2c.dev/
- Block explorer: https://explorer.maya2c.dev/
- Faucet: https://faucet.maya2c.dev/
- Public JSON-RPC: https://rpc.maya2c.dev/rpc
